The @theme blocks, shared by both stylesheets: index.css emits them and console.css imports them as a reference.
Hand-parsed on purpose: the lockout gate answers first, and a malformed /login body gets a terse 400 that spends no lockout budget; zod's issue list would echo the submitted password.
Hand-parsed on purpose, in /refresh and in the logout handler both routes share: the body is optional (the cookie wins), and a malformed one is no credential, a 401 or a 204, never a 400.
Hand-parsed on purpose: the registration lockout gate answers first, and a malformed body gets a terse 400 that spends no registration budget.
Hand-parsed on purpose: a bad /verify link answers with the HTML page a browser asked for (or JSON), never a bare 400.
Hand-parsed on purpose: the session check and the lockout gate answer first, and a malformed body spends no lockout budget.
Hand-parsed on purpose: a malformed console login writes its audit row (console.login.failed, reason malformed) before the 400.
Hand-parsed on purpose: a malformed client credential is a 401 invalid_client, never a 400.
Hand-parsed on purpose: a malformed body from an authenticated app fails closed to a 200 { active: false }, never a 400.
Hand-parsed on purpose: a malformed body is a refusal (invalid_body), audited and counted against the notify limiter, answered 200 { sent: false }.
Hand-parsed on purpose: a bad interaction uid renders the provider's expired page, not a JSON 400; oidc/ keeps its shape.
The JWKS is serialised once at boot and sent as a string with its own media type (application/jwk-set+json); Fastify never runs a response schema on a string reply.
The OpenID Connect provider's raw mount: the request is handed to oidc-provider through reply.hijack(), so no Fastify schema applies to it.

The vendored library's one fallback read of AUTH_TRUSTED_PROXIES, only when the app passes no trustedProxies option; the library has no config.ts, and apps vendor it as a bundle.

The vendored library's wardClientOptionsFromEnv defaults its env argument to process.env, so an app that passes none reads its own WARD_OIDC_* settings; the library has no config.ts, and apps vendor it as a bundle.

No buildTestApp: the tests build the real app with buildApp() (decision: integration tests drive the real buildApp), and a feature's own tests build a bare Fastify through testFastify(), which sets the compilers and the error plugin as buildApp does.
